inputs.title: The Thing
inputs.logline: When Bo’s big tail betrays how hard it is to meet new friends, Keen and Aida help him discover that the very thing he wants to hide may be the first thing everyone loves.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen attempts an exaggerated stealth mission toward Fuzzby’s honeycomb, but every crunchy step and snore-bubble pop makes the world more awake than he wants it to be. The beat is about borrowed boldness meeting tiny physical resistance.
beats.want: Keen wants to get close enough to take honey without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that rushing toward what he wants is not the same as being ready or unseen.
beats.kidRead: Keen is being silly-sneaky and the sleeping bee might wake up any second.
beats.adultRead: A child’s confidence is charmingly exposed by his own body and the environment; he is not as invisible as he thinks.
beats.emotionalIntent: Light suspense and giggly anticipation, with the honeycomb as the forbidden prize.

beats.adultRead: The comedy is the impossibility of controlling every tell; Keen’s cover is doomed because he is still a kid in a too-big plan.
beats.emotionalIntent: Build the laugh through anticipation, release it with the sneeze, then button it with Fuzzby’s sleepy authority.

beats.need: She needs to trust the quiet signal and make room for someone else’s fear without taking over.
beats.kidRead: A magic bowl shows a squirrel who keeps packing but does not go anywhere.
beats.adultRead: The repetition is instantly recognizable as a child trying to make a hard transition feel controllable.
beats.emotionalIntent: Quiet wonder with a small ache under it; the vision should feel intimate, not flashy.

beats.storyBeat: Inside the hollow tree, Bo answers his offscreen Mum but bargains with time and his conker, delaying the Learning Circle by making “a minute” stretch absurdly. The safe room is cosy, but it is also a trap of postponement.
beats.want: Bo wants to put off leaving while sounding like he still intends to go.
beats.need: He needs to be witnessed in the stuck place instead of left alone with the loop.
beats.kidRead: Bo keeps finding reasons not to go yet, and his conker is like his little helper.
beats.adultRead: The offscreen parent call captures the morning-transition ache: encouragement from another room cannot cross the threshold for him.
beats.emotionalIntent: Tender comic avoidance; keep it small, domestic and recognisable.

vision.premise: Bo is due at the Learning Circle for the first time, but every step toward the door makes his tail poof with worry. Keen’s playful curiosity and Aida’s quiet truth help him move toward the group one step at a time, until the tail he feared becomes his way in.
vision.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo go to the Learning Circle without having to hide the part of himself that gives him away?
vision.theme: Belonging begins when the thing you were trying to hide is gently witnessed and welcomed.
vision.externalJourney: Keen fails to steal honey, is redirected by Aida, visits Bo’s hollow tree, walks him through the woods, helps him arrive at the Learning Circle, and returns home to find Fuzzby attempting his own honey heist.
vision.internalJourney: Bo moves from delaying and controlling every detail to taking a visible step forward with his worry still present, then letting his tail become play instead of proof that something is wrong with him.
vision.relationshipChanges: Bo and Keen shift from strangers at a doorway to easy friends; Bo and Aida move from cautious distance to shared truth; Bo and the Learning Circle group move from imagined judgement to delighted acceptance. Fuzzby and Zenny provide the comic echo: being ridiculous and still belonging.
vision.emotionalCurve: Playful mischief opens the episode, then narrows into Bo’s held-at-the-door worry. The woods give relief through play, dip again at the log, soften through Aida’s honesty, glow into the walk forward, burst into group joy, and settle in a warm, lightly comic garden coda.
vision.comedyCurve: The comedy starts with stealth, snore bubbles, pollen and sneezes; turns into tail-poof escalation and Keen’s useless-tail demonstration; blooms into group delight at the Learning Circle; and ends with Fuzzby’s flower-disguise failure and Zenny’s tiny crack of amusement.
vision.setupPayoffMap: The untouched honeycomb and Fuzzby’s “never ever” return in the final garden heist. Bo’s conker and repeated packing plant his need for control. The tail’s first unwanted poof pays off as a chosen game in the woods and then as the Learning Circle’s delight. Aida’s vision of Bo unable to move pays off in Bo walking forward under pink and blue light. “Every single time” moves from Aida’s truth to Bo’s own action phrase.
vision.visualMotifs: Closed/open thresholds, paws holding objects too tightly, Bo’s tail expanding beyond his control, the forest path as a visible line between home and belonging, and the honeycomb as comic temptation that remains untouched.
vision.sonicMotifs: Crunching steps, snore-bubble pops, sneeze blasts, the shave-and-a-haircut knock, tail POOFs, Aida’s bowl tone, rose and aquamarine glow tones, group cheers, and Zenny’s bookend Ommmm.
vision.climax: Aida and Keen each offer their crystal truth, pink and blue light join on the forest path, and Bo takes one step, then another, toward the Learning Circle.
vision.resolution: At the Learning Circle, Bo’s tail poofs in front of everyone and is met with wonder, cheering and play; later, he draws with Keen while Aida watches his settled belonging from the edge of the clearing.
vision.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, giggly relief: the child feels the fun of the fluffy tail, while the adult feels the ache of a child being welcomed without needing to edit himself.

northStar.surfaceStory: Sunny bursts into the Learning Circle with a huge welcome, Luna gently reins in the energy, and Bo tries to sit carefully enough that his tail will not betray him. It poofs in front of everyone; the silence he feared is broken not by rejection, but by Misty and Ah-mee wanting to see it again, turning the tail into a shared game.
northStar.universalTruth: The part a child is most scared everyone will notice can become the first doorway into belonging when the room responds with wonder instead of judgement.
northStar.childClearWant: Bo wants to sit in the circle and not have his tail make a scene.
northStar.emotionalNeed: Bo needs to feel that being noticed for the thing he hides does not mean being left out.
northStar.falseBeliefUnderPressure: If my tail pops out in front of everyone, they will think I am strange and I will not belong here.
northStar.relationshipEngine: Sunny’s welcome is too big for Bo to hide inside; Luna’s pause makes the room safe enough to hear what happens; Misty’s curious question and Ah-mee’s delighted request reframe the poof from embarrassment into invitation. The group does not fix Bo — their honest curiosity lets him choose to stay visible.
northStar.ordinaryLifeTruth: A new child walking into a group often believes the safest plan is to make their body, voice, and differences smaller. The healing is not a speech; it is the first moment another child treats the difference like play.
northStar.sceneTurn: The feared silence after the tail poof turns when Misty asks, “Can it do that again?” — the same attention Bo expected to hurt him becomes attention that includes him.
audienceJourney: Giggle at Sunny’s unstoppable welcome rush.
Feel Bo’s small alarm as the room’s attention lands on him.
Hold breath when the tail poofs and everyone sees it.
Expect embarrassment or laughter at Bo.
Feel relief when Misty’s curiosity is gentle, not mean.
Delight as Ah-mee turns the tail into a group game.

northStar.finalAfterFeeling: Warm, relieved, and still a little tender: Bo has not become instantly confident, but he has taken one visible step toward belonging.
northStar.dialogueSubtractionOpportunity: Do not add any reassurance such as “It’s okay,” “We like your tail,” or “You belong here.” The group’s softened faces, forward leans, delighted silence, and Bo choosing to count down carry that meaning. Do not explain Bo’s fear; his careful sit, held breath, and wait after the poof tell it.
northStar.environmentPressure: The Learning Circle itself creates the pressure: everyone faces inward, the open center makes Bo visible, and sitting down requires him to manage the very tail he is trying to hide. The room is not wallpaper; its circular attention turns a private worry into a public moment.

tapestry.physicalMotif: The tail-poof is the emotional truth made physical: first an unwanted betrayal, then an invited bit of play. Bo’s body moves from careful containment to tiny chosen showmanship.
tapestry.sonicMotif: Sunny’s breathless word-rush gives way to Luna’s small reset, then to a held hush around the poof. The key sound is the soft comic poof followed by the absence of ridicule; Bo’s “3,2,1 …” becomes the first sound of him participating on purpose.

During the poof, hold the light clear and honest rather than dramatic, so there is nowhere for Bo to hide. After Misty and Ah-mee respond, allow the warmth of the circle to feel shared rather than spotlighting him alone.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen attempts an exaggerated stealth mission toward Fuzzby’s honeycomb, but every crunchy step and snore-bubble pop makes the world more awake than he wants it to be. The beat is about borrowed boldness meeting tiny physical resistance.
beats.want: Keen wants to get close enough to take honey without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that rushing toward what he wants is not the same as being ready or unseen.
beats.kidRead: Keen is being silly-sneaky and the sleeping bee might wake up any second.
beats.adultRead: A child’s confidence is charmingly exposed by his own body and the environment; he is not as invisible as he thinks.
beats.emotionalIntent: Light suspense and giggly anticipation, with the honeycomb as the forbidden prize.

treatments.name: Treatment 1 — The Circle Becomes a Spotlight, Then a Playground
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience first feels the Learning Circle as too open, too bright, and too focused on Bo: funny because Sunny is hilariously unstoppable, tense because every friendly face accidentally makes Bo more visible. The tail-poof lands as the tiny public catastrophe Bo has been dreading. The release comes when the same circle of attention stops feeling like a spotlight and becomes a shared game.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Bo governs the scene. The camera and staging live inside his careful hope: he wants to join without becoming the subject. Sunny’s welcome is not threatening, but to Bo it arrives like a parade aimed directly at his hiding place. Luna’s “Sunny. Breathe.” briefly gives him a safer pocket of air. The feared silence after the poof is held through Bo’s waiting body before Misty and Ah-mee gently change its meaning.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Comic mechanism: escalating overcommitment plus concealment → revelation. Bo’s careful sitting is too careful; the more he tries to manage the tail, the more the body announces him. Sunny’s welcome supplies the first comic blast; Luna’s tiny correction makes the contrast funny. Dramatic mechanism: public attention is transformed from exposure into invitation without anyone explaining it.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Sunny enters with full-body friendliness: words tumbling faster than her breath, momentum spilling into the circle as if welcome itself has feet. Luna barely enlarges her action; the power is in the small reset and the clean timing of “Sunny. Breathe.” Sunny obeys with visible effort on “Right. Breathing.” Bo’s body is held-in: tiny adjustments, breath trapped, paws choosing where to sit as if every inch might set off the tail. After the poof, he freezes rather than fleeing. Misty leans forward with soft curiosity, not excitement at his expense. Ah-mee’s delight is smaller-bodied and open-hearted, an invitation rather than a demand. Bo’s “3,2,1 …” is nervous participation: he is not suddenly confident, but he chooses to be seen.
treatments.visualGrammar: The scene begins with the circle reading as a ring of attention around an exposed center. Compositions use curved foreground edges, partial shoulders, and small gaps between seated friends to make Bo feel watched without making the others unkind. When the poof happens, the frame clears and simplifies: Bo and the tail have nowhere to hide. After Misty’s question, the visual grammar softens into shared spacing; the circle no longer traps Bo in the middle, it gathers around the game.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera is allied with Bo’s threshold experience. It does not safely observe from outside the circle; it enters with him, discovers faces as he discovers them, and lets Sunny’s welcome rush toward the lens. During the silence it refuses to escape Bo’s discomfort. Once Misty reframes the moment, the camera’s allegiance widens to the group, allowing Bo to experience attention as shared rather than aimed.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Sunny is the moving force; Bo is controlled stillness under pressure. Luna creates the first meaningful still point. The poof is the body breaking Bo’s stillness against his will. The post-poof hush is the scene’s held breath. Misty’s small forward lean is the turn: minimal movement carrying maximum kindness. By the end, Bo initiates movement through the countdown, so stillness becomes chosen anticipation rather than fear.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: The Learning Circle is active pressure. Its open center makes Bo visible; the curved seating gives every eyeline a destination. Early depth places friendly faces in layers around him, so belonging and scrutiny are visually the same thing. After “Can it do that again?” the same depth becomes warmer: faces are still present, but their forward leans create a bridge rather than a wall. Clear daytime light keeps the moment honest; Bo cannot hide in moodiness or shadow.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Start fast with Sunny’s breathless verbal tumble, then a precise Luna brake. Let Sunny’s “Right. Breathing.” create a small comic after-bounce. Slow sharply as Bo sits; every micro-adjustment should feel like it might cause the poof. The poof interrupts the over-control. Hold the silence long enough for children to wonder if trouble is coming and adults to feel Bo’s fear. Misty’s line breaks the hold gently. Ah-mee’s “Do it again!” lifts the rhythm into play. Bo’s countdown ends the scene on chosen suspense.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by changed pressure and changed point of view, never by coverage habit. Early cuts may be quick because Sunny’s energy changes the room. As Bo sits, fewer cuts: the unbrokenness makes his body management feel fragile. The post-poof hold must not be escaped until the emotional meaning changes. After Misty’s question, cutting can open the circle because the power has shifted from Bo being examined to Bo being invited.
treatments.openingImage: Bo at the edge of the Learning Circle, framed through the curved opening between seated friends, trying to enter as if the empty center were a very loud place.
treatments.closingImage: Bo still inside the same circle, small but visible, counting “3,2,1 …” while the group waits with delighted gentleness for the tail to become a game he chose.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not make this a safe classroom two-shot scene. If we park outside the circle, we lose Bo’s exposure. The camera must feel the circle’s attention physically: faces near lens, curved occlusions, Bo briefly swallowed by friendly bodies, then isolated by the open center. The challenge is to make kindness feel overwhelming before it becomes comforting.

treatments.name: Treatment 2 — Sunny’s Comet Tail, Bo’s Tiny Orbit
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience rides the comedy of a room that moves too fast for a newcomer. Sunny is a comet of welcome; Bo is the small object trying not to wobble out of orbit. The tail-poof becomes the unexpected collision between big social energy and Bo’s private control. The relief is not calmness, but play: the room’s energy finally includes Bo instead of sweeping over him.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The scene is governed by the room’s energy as Bo experiences it. Sunny’s friendliness is sincere and excessive; Luna’s intervention is the first sign that this circle has brakes as well as brightness. Bo’s inner fear is revealed through the contrast between the group’s loose, social motion and his precise, over-managed sitting. Misty and Ah-mee do not soothe him verbally; they redirect the room’s energy toward wonder.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Comic mechanism: movement against stillness. Sunny’s welcome has too much momentum; Bo’s careful stillness becomes funnier and more fragile beside it. Secondary mechanism: status change. The tail begins as Bo’s embarrassing betrayer, then becomes the circle’s most interesting game piece. Dramatic mechanism: the community’s rhythm adjusts around the newcomer instead of demanding he match it immediately.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Sunny’s line is performed as a single joyful spill, with the cake thought repeatedly hijacking the introduction. Her body should almost outrun the sentence. Luna’s correction is gentle but exact: no scolding, just a small hand on the room’s volume knob. Sunny’s “Right. Breathing.” is an earnest attempt to perform breathing correctly, which is funny because she is still Sunny. Bo times his sit like a delicate landing, pausing between choices. His tail-poof catches him before he can compose a face. Misty’s “Can it do that again?” is not loud; it is genuine discovery. Ah-mee’s “Do it again!” carries delighted empathy, with her whole small body leaning into the possibility. Bo’s countdown is the first moment he lets the room’s rhythm pass through him.
treatments.visualGrammar: The scene uses energetic arcs and interruptions rather than static circle symmetry. Sunny’s path bends through the space, creating a visible current that Bo tries to step around. Luna’s pause temporarily straightens the visual chaos. Bo’s careful sit is staged as an attempted soft landing in a room still humming from Sunny. After the poof, the composition flips: the tail becomes the visual center, and the room’s arcs now point toward shared anticipation rather than accidental pressure.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera is not fixed to Bo alone; it behaves like the room’s social energy. It is tugged by Sunny, steadied by Luna, then becomes hypersensitive to Bo’s tiny movements. When the tail poofs, the camera does not overreact with a gag zoom or panic; it lets the sound and stillness do the work. With Misty and Ah-mee, the camera follows curiosity, not spectacle.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Movement dominates at first: Sunny’s verbal and physical rush, the circle responding, Bo receiving too much too quickly. Luna creates a pocket of stillness. Bo then tries to live entirely inside that stillness, overdoing it until the tail breaks the rule. The silence after the poof is a suspended orbit. The final countdown restores movement as shared anticipation: everyone is still, but now because they are playing with Bo, not judging him.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Use the Learning Circle as a social solar system: Sunny crosses near, Luna anchors at a stabilizing distance, Bo approaches the center cautiously, and Misty and Ah-mee become the gentle pull that keeps him from drifting away after embarrassment. Depth should keep the circle legible without assigning permanent sides. Background faces are not wallpaper; their softened attention is the pressure and then the comfort.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Begin at Sunny-speed, almost too fast, then let Luna cut the tempo in half with two words. Sunny’s breathing beat gives a comic reset. Bo’s sit slows the scene into tiny suspense: the audience watches for the body to betray him. The poof is quick and soft, followed by a silence that feels enormous compared with the sound. Misty’s question lands like a small bell. Ah-mee adds the childlike release. Bo’s “3,2,1 …” creates a new rhythm the group can join.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: The edit should feel musical: fast tumbling phrases for Sunny, a clean rest for Luna, slowed sustained notes for Bo, then a gentle pickup into the group game. Cut only when the room’s rhythm changes hands. Avoid automatic reaction cutting around the circle; the post-poof silence is stronger if the audience feels everyone present without being marched face-to-face through each response.
treatments.openingImage: Sunny’s welcome rush bends the Learning Circle’s calm shape, with Bo just inside the room’s social current, trying not to be knocked into visibility.
treatments.closingImage: The circle held in shared anticipation, Bo conducting the next poof with “3,2,1 …” as if his once-unwanted tail has become the room’s new rhythm.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: The risk is turning the circle into a polite diagram. I want the camera to feel pulled by social gravity: Sunny can drag the frame off its intended calm, Luna can stop it, Bo can make it cautious. The challenge is readable geography without fixed lanes — the audience always knows the circle, but the composition keeps changing as emotional gravity changes.

treatments.name: Treatment 3 — The Sound of Being Noticed
treatments.audienceExperience: The scene is built around sound and silence: Sunny’s flood of words, Luna’s breath reset, the tiny private noises of Bo trying to sit invisibly, the soft poof, then the enormous quiet where Bo expects rejection. Children enjoy the suspense of waiting for the funny tail to happen again; adults feel the ache of a child listening for whether the room will laugh at him or welcome him.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Bo’s listening governs the scene. The world is friendly, but every sound tells him how visible he is. Sunny’s voice fills all the space he hoped to slip through. Luna’s “Sunny. Breathe.” opens a quiet path. The tail-poof is not staged as a huge explosion; it is devastating because the room goes quiet after it. Misty and Ah-mee heal the moment by changing what that silence means: not judgement, but wonder waiting for an answer.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Comic mechanism: silence replacing dialogue. The funniest and most tender part is the quiet after the poof: everyone saw it, nobody says the cruel thing Bo fears, and the audience hangs in that gap. Secondary mechanism: anticipation → reversal. Bo anticipates social disaster; the reversal is gentle curiosity. Dramatic mechanism: a feared sound becomes an invited sound.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Sunny’s welcome is all breath and overflow, with the cake tangent arriving as if it has been waiting impatiently inside her. Luna’s line should be low-effort and perfectly timed; she does not crush Sunny, she gives the room back its ears. Sunny’s “Right. Breathing.” is audible self-management. Bo’s performance is concentrated in listening: a glance at each sound, a held breath before sitting, a tiny wince at the poof, then the stillness of waiting. Misty’s question must sound like wonder, not a challenge. Ah-mee’s request is immediate delight, but gentle enough that Bo can accept it. Bo’s “3,2,1 …” is barely brave, which is why it matters.
treatments.visualGrammar: The visuals support an acoustic idea. Frames emphasize mouths, breaths, paws pausing, ears and eyelines registering small sounds, and the empty air around Bo after the poof. The scene avoids noisy visual busyness during the silence; clear light and simple spacing let the audience hear the emotional gap. After the group responds, the frame regains little movements: leaning, smiling, waiting, counting.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera behaves like an attentive listener. It goes where the next meaningful sound changes Bo’s body: Sunny’s rush, Luna’s breath command, Sunny trying to breathe, Bo’s careful sit, the poof, Misty’s curious question, Ah-mee’s delighted request, Bo’s countdown. It does not chase spectacle; it attends to the tiny sound that alters belonging.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Motion is reduced in importance as the scene progresses. Sunny starts with full kinetic noise. Luna pares the room down. Bo’s sit is slow enough that small cloth, floor, and breath details become suspenseful. The poof creates a small sound followed by large stillness. Misty and Ah-mee restart the room with minimal forward motion. The final countdown makes stillness active: everyone waits because Bo is leading the moment.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: The Learning Circle becomes an acoustic bowl. Early, Sunny’s voice seems to fill it from every direction. When Luna slows her, the space gains air. Bo’s careful sit is placed so the open center amplifies the poof and the following quiet. Depth is used to show listening: faces held at different distances, all turned toward the same small sound. Daylight remains clear and truthful, with warmth increasing through group attention rather than a dramatic lighting change.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm moves from verbal abundance to breath, from breath to tiny body suspense, from poof to silence, from silence to invitation. Sunny’s line should feel almost impossible to contain; Luna’s two words create the first reset. Bo’s careful sitting stretches time. The poof is quick. The hush is the nadir. Misty’s “Can it do that again?” is the emotional turn. Ah-mee’s “Do it again!” supplies the release. Bo’s “3,2,1 …” leaves the audience leaning in for the next sound.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts follow sound events and listening shifts. Resist cutting merely to show every face reacting. A held frame after the poof is essential: the audience must sit in the same unanswered quiet as Bo. After Misty speaks, cuts may become warmer and more inclusive, but still sparing; the scene’s power is that nobody needs to explain what just changed.
treatments.openingImage: The Learning Circle in bright day, with Sunny’s voice rushing into the open air before Bo has found a quiet way to belong in it.
treatments.closingImage: Bo listening to his own small countdown, the circle silent again — but this time the silence is eager, warm, and shared.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: If we over-animate the poof or over-cover reactions, we destroy the scene’s central sound: the silence after. The camera must be brave enough to hold on Bo when nothing is ‘happening’ except him listening for rejection. The challenge is making quiet visually active through breath, eyelines, and tiny body tension, not through decorative camera movement.

treatmentSelection.selectedTreatment: Combined treatment — The Sound of Being Noticed in the Circle
combinedFrom: Treatment 3 — The Sound of Being Noticed
Treatment 1 — The Circle Becomes a Spotlight, Then a Playground
treatmentSelection.governingAudienceExperience: The audience listens with Bo in the exposed center of the Learning Circle, fearing that being noticed will hurt, then feeling the same quiet turn warm when the room answers his difference with wonder.
treatmentSelection.rationale: Treatment 3 is the governing choice because it finds the scene’s deepest truth in Bo’s listening, not in the mechanics of a tail gag. The soft poof matters because of what follows: the enormous silence where Bo waits to learn whether the circle is safe. That gives children suspense and comedy, while adults feel the ache of a new child bracing for judgement. Treatment 1 should be folded in for its strong use of the Learning Circle as emotional pressure: the same circular attention first feels like a spotlight, then becomes a playground. Together, they give the scene a clear transformation from exposure to invitation without adding reassurance dialogue or explaining the feeling. Sunny’s rush, Luna’s breath reset, Bo’s held body, Misty’s gentle curiosity, and Ah-mee’s delighted request all remain character-specific. The scene becomes memorable because its biggest event is not the poof itself, but Bo choosing to count down afterward — turning the sound he feared into a sound he can share.
treatmentSelection.rejectionChecks: Selected approach rejects fixed character lanes: the circle’s emotional gravity changes as Sunny rushes, Luna steadies, Bo freezes, and Misty reframes. It rejects keeping all characters visibly covered: the audience does not need a reaction parade; presence can be felt through sound, breath, eyelines, and partial bodies. It rejects habitual action/reaction coverage and repeated close-up punctuation: the post-poof hold must stay with Bo’s unanswered listening until the meaning changes. It rejects safe camera placement outside the circle: the camera must feel the circle’s attention physically, not observe a polite classroom diagram. It rejects mechanical shot counts and generic ‘cinematic’ decoration: cuts are motivated only by shifts in sound, pressure, and belonging. Treatment 2 is not selected because its room-energy/comet-orbit idea risks letting Sunny’s motion and the group’s rhythm govern the scene more than Bo’s private fear; it is lively, but less emotionally precise than listening from inside Bo’s exposure.

beats.whatChanges: The circle shifts from open possibility into overwhelming attention: Sunny’s welcome makes Bo visible, Luna briefly creates a safer pause, then Bo’s careful control fails when the tail poofs and leaves him waiting in the exposed silence.
beats.whoDrives: Sunny drives the first pressure through unstoppable welcome; Luna briefly redirects the room; Bo drives the emotional turn by attempting to sit carefully and then freezing instead of escaping after the poof.
beats.audienceAnticipation: Children expect Sunny’s rush to be funny and then begin watching Bo’s body, waiting for the tail to give him away; adults feel the dread of the quiet after a public embarrassment.
beats.actionOrChoice: Bo tries to enter and sit as if every small movement must be managed; when the tail announces him anyway, he does not flee or cover it, but holds still inside the circle’s attention.

emotionContract.entryState: Nervous hope contained in a body trying to take up as little attention as possible.
emotionContract.pressure: The Learning Circle faces inward, Sunny’s welcome arrives too brightly to hide inside, and sitting down risks exposing the tail.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Bo chooses control: tiny placements, trapped breath, and a careful sit meant to keep the tail from becoming the subject; after the poof, his visible choice is to freeze rather than run.
emotionContract.exitState: Exposed and suspended, waiting to learn whether being noticed will hurt.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: Bo’s paws choose their place cautiously, his breath is held, his body stays over-controlled; after the poof he goes still instead of bouncing away, with the circle’s silence held on him.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The soft poof sound and the absence of immediate ridicule remain hanging in the room, unresolved.

comedyContract.setup: Bo wants to sit in the circle without his tail making a scene, while Sunny’s enormous welcome has already made quiet entry impossible.
comedyContract.expectation: If Bo is careful enough, he may pass into the group unnoticed; Sunny’s energy should settle once Luna tells her to breathe.
comedyContract.disruption: Sunny’s effortful obedience creates a tiny comic after-bounce, then Bo’s over-careful body management produces the very reveal he is trying to prevent: the tail poofs in public.
comedyContract.button: The button is not a line; it is Bo’s frozen waiting after the soft poof, with the room suddenly too quiet around the thing everyone has seen.
comedyContract.hold: Hold long enough for the audience to move from giggle to concern, but do not let any character rescue the silence before Misty’s next-beat question changes its meaning.

physicalStaging.staysVisible: Bo, the open center of the Learning Circle, and the tail must remain readable through the poof; surrounding friends can be partial bodies or close presences, but the tail reveal cannot be hidden by coverage or reaction cuts.
physicalStaging.contactAndWeight: Bo’s sit has visible weight and hesitation: small settling pressure into the circle space, paws braced, breath held; the poof breaks that containment as a soft physical expansion rather than a hard impact.
physicalStaging.payoffShape: A tiny public catastrophe: careful containment compresses into stillness, then the tail suddenly blooms into visibility, leaving Bo small and motionless beside the now-unmissable tail.
prohibitedStaging: Do not cut away from Bo at the instant of the poof.
Do not play the group as laughing at him.
Do not make the poof explosive or superheroic; it is soft, comic, and emotionally exposing.

emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: When Misty and Amie meet the tail with curiosity and delight, Bo realises he can stay visible; his costly choice is to answer with “3,2,1 …” and invite the moment again.
emotionContract.exitState: Still small and nervous, but warmed by proof that being noticed can include him.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: Bo remains in the circle, does not cover the tail, and gives the countdown himself; the group’s forward leans and delighted gentleness make attention feel shared rather than aimed at him.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The ache is not erased: Bo’s confidence is only a first step, held inside the warmer image of everyone waiting gently with him.

comedyContract.mechanism: Status change through gentle reframing: the embarrassing reveal becomes the requested trick.
comedyContract.setup: The poof has left Bo frozen in a silence he reads as possible judgement.
comedyContract.expectation: Someone may laugh at him, reject the tail, or rush to reassure him in a way that keeps him embarrassed.
comedyContract.disruption: Misty asks with genuine wonder whether it can happen again, and Amie’s delight treats the tail as play rather than problem.
comedyContract.button: Bo’s “3,2,1 …” is the button because the child who wanted not to be noticed now quietly conducts the room’s anticipation.
comedyContract.hold: Hold after the countdown begins so the audience can feel that Bo is not magically transformed; the comedy rests on his tiny brave participation, not on a loud triumph.

stagePlan.purpose: Turn the Learning Circle from possible welcome into friendly overexposure through Sunny’s unstoppable greeting, then give Bo a tiny pocket of safety when Luna slows the room.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Sunny jumps up and rushes her greeting toward Bo — “33	HI! I'm Sunny! Do you like cake? I like singing and dancing … and cake! I mean who doesn’t like cake?!?” — then spins happily until Luna’s quiet “34	Sunny. Breathe.” stops the rush and causes Sunny to take a huge breath before “Right. Breathing.”
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The laugh comes from Sunny’s escalating overcommitment meeting Luna’s minimal correction; for Bo, the welcome is kind but too bright to hide inside.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Begin inside the circle from Bo’s threshold, with curved seated bodies close to lens; let Sunny’s motion rush into the frame, then use a motivated internal cut on Luna’s small stillness because her restraint changes the room’s pressure.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Sunny is visibly trying to hold still after a huge breath, and the circle has paused just enough for Bo to attempt sitting.

stagePlan.purpose: Make Bo’s attempt to join a fragile body-management suspense, then let the tail-poof turn private fear into public exposure.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo lowers himself onto a cushion with over-careful control, and the careful sit causes his tail to suddenly poof huge where everyone can see it.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: Concealment becomes revelation: the harder Bo tries not to make the tail the subject, the more clearly the body announces him.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Stay with Bo rather than cutting away; simplify the frame around the open center so the tail and Bo have nowhere to hide, and protect the soft poof plus the immediate silence.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo is frozen beside the unmissable tail in the exposed center of the circle while everyone has seen it.

stagePlan.purpose: Transform the feared silence into gentle curiosity, then into a shared game Bo chooses to enter.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Misty’s “36	Can it do that again?” invites the tail-poof again, bigger, and everyone cheers; Amie’s “37	Do it again!” lifts the moment into play, and Bo answers with “3,2,1 …” before the tail becomes the group’s delight and tickles Kit into giggles.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The attention Bo expected to hurt him becomes attention that includes him; the embarrassing reveal changes status into the requested trick.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: After Misty’s question changes the meaning, open the frame from Bo’s isolation into shared spacing, allowing partial faces and forward leans to bridge toward him without crowding him.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo remains small but visible inside the circle, preparing another tail-poof while the group waits with delighted gentleness.

shots.purpose: Carry the full causal arc from overwhelming welcome, to public tail-poof exposure, to the same attention becoming Bo’s first shared game.
shots.audienceExperience: The audience feels the circle’s kindness as too bright for Bo, holds the worried silence after the poof with him, then relaxes as curiosity and delight turn the spotlight into play.
shots.openingImage: Bo at the edge of the Learning Circle, seen through the curved gap between seated friends as the empty center opens in front of him.
shots.principalPerformance: Bo begins with nervous hope contained in tiny controlled placements, freezes after the poof instead of fleeing, then chooses a small, still-nervous showman’s start for the next poof; Sunny’s friendliness spills forward, Luna’s minimal correction briefly steadies the room, Misty and Amie reframe attention as invitation.
shots.cameraRelationship: Allied with Bo’s threshold experience: the camera lives inside the circle rather than outside it, lets Sunny’s welcome rush at Bo, refuses to escape the post-poof discomfort, then widens its allegiance only when the group’s response becomes safe.
shots.physicalOrEmotionalChange: Bo’s tail changes from hidden liability to shared play object, and Bo changes from trying to enter unseen to inviting the circle to watch with him.
shots.closingImage: Bo seated inside the same circle, one paw lifted in a tiny conducting gesture, the fluffy tail poised behind him while the surrounding friends lean forward with gentle anticipation.
shots.transitionReason: The shot completes the scene’s transformation from exposure to invitation; remaining continuous beyond this landing would dilute Bo’s first chosen visibility, while a cut after the held anticipation preserves it as the scene’s final proof.

cinematographyContract.emotionalDistanceEnd: Still intimate but less trapped, with the group’s forward leans creating a shared play space around Bo.

cinematographyContract.composition: Curved foreground occlusions and small gaps early; cleared center for the poof; softened ring with bridging faces after Misty’s question.
cinematographyContract.depthStrategy: Early depth layers friendly faces around Bo as both belonging and scrutiny; after the turn, those same layers lean forward as connection rather than a wall.
cinematographyContract.cameraBehavior: Enter with Bo, absorb Sunny’s rush, lock down for Luna’s brake, stay on Bo through the sit and hush, then ease open only after the meaning of attention changes.
cinematographyContract.focusStrategy: Begin with Bo’s gap and Sunny’s approach competing; hold clean focus on Luna’s stillness for the reset; protect Bo and the tail during the poof, then allow gentle shared focus across the nearer group.

cinematographyContract.paletteFunction: Sunny clearing colors begin bright and slightly exposing for Bo; the same warm palette becomes inclusive as the circle’s spacing changes.
cinematographyContract.performanceVisibility: Bo’s paws, breath, tail space, freeze, and tiny conducting gesture must remain readable; reactions matter only when they reframe him with curiosity and delight.
cinematographyContract.editorialPurpose: One continuous provider unit preserves the cause-and-effect of Bo’s fear being tested and redefined without breaking the post-poof held breath.
cinematographyContract.memorableLandingImage: Bo small but present in the circle, initiating the next tail-poof as the group waits with him instead of at him.
cinematographyContract.providerInstruction: Start inside the Learning Circle through seated foreground curves on Bo’s entrance; let Sunny rush toward the lens, brake on Luna’s stillness, hold Bo’s careful sit until the soft tail-poof clears the frame into silence, then ease wider as.

performanceBudget.rationale: The full arc fits within 30 seconds only if kept lean: Sunny’s fast welcome, Luna’s precise brake, Bo’s careful sit, the poof hush, and the gentle reframe are all causally connected. Splitting would weaken the essential transformation because the feared silence must carry directly into Misty’s question.

storyIntent.narrativeFunction: Introduce Bo’s hidden fear inside the group and convert the tail-poof from public embarrassment into the first shared game.
storyIntent.primaryAudienceFeeling: Protective suspense for Bo as he becomes visible.
storyIntent.secondaryAudienceFeeling: Relief and delight when the room’s curiosity proves gentle.
storyIntent.outerAction: Sunny welcomes too brightly, Luna slows her, Bo sits and the tail poofs, Misty and Amie invite it again, and Bo chooses to count the next one in.
storyIntent.innerAction: Bo tests whether he can belong without exposing the hidden part, then discovers exposure does not send him away.
storyIntent.performanceDirection: Play Bo as contained and listening; every small paw placement is a decision, the freeze is fear, and the countdown is brave participation without sudden confidence.
storyIntent.mutedRead: With sound off, Sunny’s rush, Luna’s stilling gesture, Bo’s careful sit, the sudden tail bloom, the hush, Misty’s soft lean, Amie’s delighted request, and Bo’s tiny conducting gesture still tell the transformation.
storyIntent.environmentPressure: The inward-facing circle and open center turn sitting down into a public act; friendly faces in layers make belonging and scrutiny visually inseparable until the reframe.
storyIntent.soundStory: Sunny’s word-rush crowds the air, Luna creates a clean pause, the soft poof and following quiet carry Bo’s fear, then cheers and giggles become acceptance through play rather than reassurance.
storyIntent.motifUse: The tail-poof is the signed physical motif: first an involuntary betrayal of Bo’s need, then an invited game he helps begin.
storyIntent.thoughtChangeAndCut: The governing thought changes from “If they see it, I am unsafe” to “They are waiting with me”; cut only after that thought has become visible in Bo’s chosen participation.
storyIntent.mustUnderstand: Bo wanted not to be noticed, the tail made him visible anyway, and the group’s response is wonder rather than judgement.
storyIntent.mustNotKnowYet: Bo is not fully confident or cured; this is only the first proof that the circle may have room for all of him.
storyIntent.reactionBeat: Misty’s gentle curiosity is the meaning-changing reaction; other reactions support the turn but must not become mockery or automatic coverage.
storyIntent.relationshipDistance: At first Bo is separated by the exposed center; by the end the group is still around him but visually bridged by soft forward leans.
storyIntent.relationshipPowerDynamic: Sunny accidentally overpowers Bo with welcome, Luna briefly regulates the room, then Misty and Amie hand agency back to Bo by asking rather than fixing.
storyIntent.touchOrAvoidance: No one grabs or fixes Bo or the tail; Kit’s tickle is incidental delight from the tail’s reach, not invasion.
storyIntent.eyelineRule: Early eyelines converge on Bo and make him feel watched; after Misty’s question, eyelines share attention between Bo and the tail as a game.
storyIntent.silhouetteRead: Bo’s small body beside the huge poofed tail must read instantly: a tiny public catastrophe becoming a tiny chosen performance.
storyIntent.silenceRule: Protect the silence immediately after the first poof; no reassurance, score swell, or reaction cut should rescue it before Misty speaks.
storyIntent.scoreInstruction: Keep score absent or very light under Sunny’s rush; thin out for the hush so the poof and quiet can land, then allow a small playful lift after the group’s curiosity turns the moment.

shots.physicalPerformance: Sunny bursts upright and floods the circle with bouncing welcome, overshooting the space before Luna’s tiny stilling presence reins the room in. Bo enters through that pause with braced paws and trapped breath, lowers onto the cushion too carefully, and the tail blooms huge beside him; he freezes instead of escaping. Misty’s soft forward lean changes the silence, Ah-mee’s open delight lifts it into play, and Bo stays seated with a tiny leading paw gesture as the group waits with him.
shots.animationTiming: Fast spill for Sunny, clean held beat for Luna’s reset, then slow compression through Bo’s sit. The first poof is soft and sudden, followed by a protected hush. After Misty’s lean, timing warms into gentle group anticipation; Bo’s final gesture stays small, not triumphant.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Bo wants to join without becoming the subject; the shot tests that fear by making his hidden tail public, then lets him discover that the group’s attention can wait with him instead of closing in on him.

phases.observableAction: Sunny springs up from the seated ring, bounces toward Bo’s gap, twirls with excess momentum, and then visibly fights to contain one last after-bounce when the room steadies.
Bo places his paws carefully, lowers onto the cushion in tiny controlled increments, compresses his body around the tail space, and then goes rigid as the tail expands into full view beside him.
Misty leans forward from her place with soft curiosity, keeping her body low and open so the nearby attention shifts toward the tail without crowding Bo.
Bo remains seated, uncovers enough to lift one small paw in a conducting gesture, and leaves space behind him for the tail as the surrounding ring leans in gently.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Sunny’s forward momentum makes the open center feel too exposed; the room’s brief stillness gives Bo a chance to sit. Bo’s over-controlled lowering compresses his body until the tail expands visibly, and his freeze leaves the result hanging in the open. Misty’s soft lean redirects nearby bodies from staring at Bo to sharing curiosity about the tail; Bo’s lifted paw then gives the group a clear cue to wait with him.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo changes from a body trying to disappear into a body that stays visible long enough to invite the next tail moment himself.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: End on Bo small but present inside the circle, one paw lifted in a tiny lead-in, tail poised behind him, with the group’s gentle forward leans reading as shared anticipation rather than judgement.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: Keep room for Sunny’s secondary bounce, Luna’s tiny stillness, Bo’s breath and paw tremors, Misty’s micro-lean, Ah-mee’s small delighted opening, and the tail’s soft follow-through; do not over-choreograph the hush or make Bo suddenly confident.

comedyStaging.staysVisible: Bo, the open center of the Learning Circle, and the tail must remain readable through the poof; surrounding friends can be partial bodies or close presences, but the tail reveal cannot be hidden by coverage or reaction cuts.
comedyStaging.contactAndWeight: Bo’s sit has visible weight and hesitation: small settling pressure into the circle space, paws braced, breath held; the poof breaks that containment as a soft physical expansion rather than a hard impact.
comedyStaging.payoffShape: A tiny public catastrophe: careful containment compresses into stillness, then the tail suddenly blooms into visibility, leaving Bo small and motionless beside the now-unmissable tail.
prohibitedStaging: Do not cut away from Bo at the instant of the poof.
Do not play the group as laughing at him.
Do not make the poof explosive or superheroic; it is soft, comic, and emotionally exposing.

executionPolicy.default: Use one 4-30s Seedance unit when it has one clear job and compact stage grammar.
executionPolicy.splitWhen: Split protected units for dense physical comedy, exact reveals, route-sensitive causality, major geography changes, or more than one competing camera job.
executionPolicy.emotionalContinuity: Quiet emotional beats in the same place with the same cast should stay in one longer unit up to 30s unless the cut protects a concrete new reference, geography, object handoff, point of view or complexity boundary.
executionPolicy.continuity: Every unit must end on a usable held handoff frame of about 1s; the next unit starts from that approved frame.
executionPolicy.music: For split production units, render Seedance with dialogue/foley only and generate one ElevenLabs scene-level music cue after stitch so score continuity does not drift.

productionDetail.continuityOut: The shot leaves Bo seated inside the Learning Circle with the tail no longer hidden, one paw raised in a small cue as the group waits with gentle anticipation rather than judgement.

voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Already spring-loaded with friendliness, bursting upright before the thought is fully organized.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Still delighted, but hovering on the edge of needing help to slow down.
voicePerformances.pace: Fast spill, almost one breath too many; only the cake tangent gets a little extra bounce.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Tumbling, puppyish run-on rhythm; thoughts arrive as she says them.
voicePerformances.pauses: Tiny delighted catch before “and cake!” to make the second cake a discovery, not a list item.
voicePerformances.breaths: Start with a bright intake; run close to breathless by the final question.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Bo begins with nervous hope contained in tiny controlled placements, freezes after the poof instead of fleeing, then chooses a small, still-nervous showman’s start for the next poof; Sunny’s friendliness spills forward, Luna’s minimal correction briefly steadies the room, Misty and Amie reframe attention as invitation.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Sunny bursts upright and floods the circle with bouncing welcome, overshooting the space before Luna’s tiny stilling presence reins the room in. Bo enters through that pause with braced paws and trapped breath, lowers onto the cushion too carefully, and the tail blooms huge beside him; he freezes instead of escaping. Misty’s soft forward lean changes the silence, Ah-mee’s open delight lifts it into play, and Bo stays seated with a tiny leading paw gesture as the group waits with him.

contract.playableIntention: Bo wants to join without becoming the subject; the shot tests that fear by making his hidden tail public, then lets him discover that the group’s attention can wait with him instead of closing in on him.

phases.observableAction: Sunny springs up from the seated ring, bounces toward Bo’s gap, twirls with excess momentum, and then visibly fights to contain one last after-bounce when the room steadies.
Bo places his paws carefully, lowers onto the cushion in tiny controlled increments, compresses his body around the tail space, and then goes rigid as the tail expands into full view beside him.
Misty leans forward from her place with soft curiosity, keeping her body low and open so the nearby attention shifts toward the tail without crowding Bo.
Bo remains seated, uncovers enough to lift one small paw in a conducting gesture, and leaves space behind him for the tail as the surrounding ring leans in gently.

Misty’s soft lean redirects nearby bodies from staring at Bo to sharing curiosity about the tail; Bo’s lifted paw then gives the group a clear cue to wait with him.

contract.requiredLanding: End on Bo small but present inside the circle, one paw lifted in a tiny lead-in, tail poised behind him, with the group’s gentle forward leans reading as shared anticipation rather than judgement.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Sunny’s forward momentum makes the open center feel too exposed; the room’s brief stillness gives Bo a chance to sit. Bo’s over-controlled lowering compresses his body until the tail expands visibly, and his freeze leaves the result hanging in the open. Misty’s soft lean redirects nearby bodies from staring at Bo to sharing curiosity about the tail; Bo’s lifted paw then gives the group a clear cue to wait with him.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo changes from a body trying to disappear into a body that stays visible long enough to invite the next tail moment himself.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: End on Bo small but present inside the circle, one paw lifted in a tiny lead-in, tail poised behind him, with the group’s gentle forward leans reading as shared anticipation rather than judgement.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: Keep room for Sunny’s secondary bounce, Luna’s tiny stillness, Bo’s breath and paw tremors, Misty’s micro-lean, Ah-mee’s small delighted opening, and the tail’s soft follow-through; do not over-choreograph the hush or make Bo suddenly confident.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Full-body friendliness that rushes toward connection under pressure.
characterTruths.playableWant: She wants the new arrival to feel welcomed immediately.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: Her welcome gets bigger than the space before she can contain it.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Bouncy rise, forward spill, happy twirl, and a visible effort to hold still after the room resets.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Another character could greet Bo, but only Sunny turns kindness into a physical parade that accidentally makes the circle feel like a spotlight.

characterTruths.canonTrait: A small squirrel whose curiosity and worry pull him toward belonging while his tail exposes what he wants to manage.
characterTruths.playableWant: He wants to sit with the group without his tail becoming the subject.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He makes smaller, more careful movements, holds breath in his body, and freezes when the tail becomes visible.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Paws close and braced, light incremental lowering, tail-driven balance, sudden stillness beside the oversized poof, then one tiny leading paw gesture.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: A bear could be shy, but only Bo’s squirrel body and expressive tail make the hidden worry become the visible event.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Trust and intuition: she reads the room and approaches feeling with gentle curiosity.
characterTruths.playableWant: She wants to meet what just happened without making Bo feel handled or fixed.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: She softens the silence by leaning toward the tail, not rushing at Bo.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Low forward tilt, open paws, quiet focus on the tail, and enough distance to leave Bo room.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Another character might cheer or reassure; Misty’s specific value is sensing that curiosity will reframe the moment more safely than rescue.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Stillness that steadies a room without taking over it.
characterTruths.playableWant: She wants Sunny’s welcome to become breathable for Bo.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: She reduces her own movement and lets one small reset change the room’s pace.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Minimal body shift, steady focus, and calm containment that makes Sunny’s after-bounce readable.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Another character would have to interrupt with more energy; Luna’s restraint works because it lowers the pressure without stealing the scene.

comedyStaging.staysVisible: Bo, the open center of the Learning Circle, and the tail must remain readable through the poof; surrounding friends can be partial bodies or close presences, but the tail reveal cannot be hidden by coverage or reaction cuts.
comedyStaging.contactAndWeight: Bo’s sit has visible weight and hesitation: small settling pressure into the circle space, paws braced, breath held; the poof breaks that containment as a soft physical expansion rather than a hard impact.
comedyStaging.payoffShape: A tiny public catastrophe: careful containment compresses into stillness, then the tail suddenly blooms into visibility, leaving Bo small and motionless beside the now-unmissable tail.
prohibitedStaging: Do not cut away from Bo at the instant of the poof.
Do not play the group as laughing at him.
Do not make the poof explosive or superheroic; it is soft, comic, and emotionally exposing.

showrunnerJudgement: PASS. The storyboard preserves the selected treatment’s central experience: Bo is not merely present at a classroom welcome; the audience is placed inside his exposed threshold, feeling kind attention become too much, then feeling that same attention soften into invitation. Sunny’s rush, Luna’s brake, Bo’s over-careful sit, the public poof, the held hush, Misty’s gentle curiosity, Amie’s delighted request, and Bo’s nervous countdown accumulate into the required emotional argument without adding reassurance or explaining the feeling.
treatmentComparison: This remains faithful to “The Circle Becomes a Spotlight, Then a Playground.” The circle is treated as active pressure rather than neutral setting; Sunny’s friendliness lands as comic overexposure; Luna’s small stillness creates the safety pocket; Bo’s careful body-management makes the poof feel like the exact tiny catastrophe he feared. Most importantly, the turn is behavioural: Misty’s question and Amie’s delight change the meaning of the attention, and Bo’s “3,2,1 …” is a costly choice to stay visible rather than a sudden confidence upgrade. The treatment’s governing POV is intact because the camera begins with Bo at the threshold, stays with him through the sit and post-poof exposure, then widens only after the group’s curiosity has earned it.
packingJudgement: Packing passes. One 29-second unit is the right production shape for this material: same location, same cast, same emotional pressure, and one continuous transformation from spotlight to playground. Splitting these beats would likely create avoidable joins and weaken the held post-poof discomfort. The unit is near-full but not padded, and the three-stage structure matches the natural pressure changes: Sunny/Luna rush-and-brake, Bo’s fragile sit and poof, then Misty/Amie/Bo reframing into play.
